The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let \(N=2100\). For a prime \(p\), write \(v_p(n)\) for the exponent of \(p\) in \(n\).

In one move, replacing \(a,b\) by \(\gcd(a,b)\) and \(\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)\) replaces the pair of exponents \((v_p(a),v_p(b))\) by \((\min(v_p(a),v_p(b)),\max(v_p(a),v_p(b)))\). Thus for every prime \(p\), the multiset of \(p\)-exponents on the board is invariant.

A stopping state is one where no move changes the board. For any two numbers \(a,b\), this means
\[
\{\gcd(a,b),\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)\}=\{a,b\}.
\]
This happens exactly when one of \(a,b\) divides the other. So the final board must be a chain under divisibility. Sorting its entries in increasing order \(x_1\le x_2\le \cdots \le x_N\), we have \(x_i\mid x_{i+1}\). Hence for each prime \(p\), the sequence \(v_p(x_1),v_p(x_2),\dots,v_p(x_N)\) is nondecreasing, and since the multiset of \(p\)-exponents is invariant from the initial board, it must be exactly the sorted list of the initial \(p\)-exponents. Thus the final multiset is uniquely determined.

It is useful to list the final board in decreasing order \(y_1\ge y_2\ge \cdots \ge y_N\). The 2026th smallest entry is the 75th largest entry, since
\[
2100-2026+1=75.
\]

For a prime \(p\), the \(j\)-th largest \(p\)-exponent in the final board is the largest \(t\) such that at least \(j\) integers among \(1,2,\dots,N\) have \(p\)-exponent at least \(t\). The number of such integers is
\[
\left\lfloor \frac{N}{p^t}\right\rfloor.
\]
So for \(N=2100\) and \(j=75\), we need
\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^t}\right\rfloor \ge 75.
\]
Because \(2100/75=28\), this is equivalent to
\[
p^t \le 28.
\]
Thus the 75th largest final entry is
\[
y_{75}=\operatorname{lcm}(1,2,\dots,28).
\]

Now factor \(\operatorname{lcm}(1,2,\dots,28)\):
\[
\operatorname{lcm}(1,2,\dots,28)
=2^4\cdot 3^3\cdot 5^2\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 13\cdot 17\cdot 19\cdot 23.
\]

Therefore the number of positive divisors is
\[
(4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)^6
=5\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot 64
=3840.
\]

\[
\boxed{3840}
\]
